name: Motivation categories
outcome_template: Ten categories, of which a hand-labelled sample of 47 external campaigns used three. The labels are written at campaign granularity and {p4_cid} of the {n_flows} flows carry an ATT&CK Campaign identifier to join them to.
dismissal: Slices on what an analyst infers rather than on what the report records, and the labels do not join to this corpus at all.
provenance: partition_decision.md; gasp_schema.md Decisions 1--2 (the 47-campaign sample is docs-record only)

name: Group-witnessed objective
outcome_template: {p3_g} of the {n_flows} flows carry an ATT&CK Group identifier and {p3_c} carry a Campaign identifier; {p3_none} are unattributed.
dismissal: More than half the corpus is unclassifiable, and the classes that do form name actors rather than objectives.

name: Terminal tactic in the dependency graph
outcome_template: {p1_exfil} exfiltration, {p1_impact} impact, {p1_both} both, {p1_neither} neither. Disagrees with the attested objective on {p1_exact} of the {n_flows} flows ({p1_any} where sharing one objective tactic counts as agreement).
dismissal: The disagreement is systematic: {p1_silent} of the {p1_exact} are reports that stop before the objective is reached, so the graph is silent where the analyst attests one. It encodes documentation truncation as attacker behaviour.

name: Objective tactic reached anywhere
outcome_template: {p7_exfil} exfiltration, {p7_impact} impact, {p7_both} both, {p7_neither} neither, counting any occurrence rather than only the terminal one. Disagrees on {p7_exact} of the {n_flows} ({p7_any} under the weaker rule).
dismissal: More forgiving than the terminal read and still structural: {p7_neither} flows reach no objective tactic and stay unclassifiable.

name: Terminal technique
outcome_template: {p2_sets} distinct terminal-technique sets across the {n_flows} flows, {p2_singletons} of them held by one flow alone; {p2_cyclic} flows are cyclic and have no terminal technique.
dismissal: Fragments to roughly one class per incident. A class of one is a single account, not a behavioural envelope. Kept as a fragmentation control.

name: Stated objective, three classes with multi-membership
outcome_template: {p5_exfil} exfiltration, {p5_impact} impact and {p5_none} no-objective memberships --- {p5_total} over {n_flows} flows, because the {p5_dual} flows pursuing both objectives are counted twice.
dismissal: The profiles stop being alternatives: a flow in two of them is weighed twice in the comparison, and the compound objective has no name of its own.

name: Stated objective, four disjoint classes
outcome_template: {a_exfil} exfiltration, {a_impact} impact, {a_both} double extortion, {a_none} no realised objective. Every flow sits in exactly one class, all {n_flows} at high audit confidence.
dismissal: Adopted: the lightest scheme that is disjoint, sources every membership from an analyst's statement, and names the compound objective.
